units.translation: For it is a man's concern; let no woman plan; what is outside.
That never again should it be a concern to rise up.
And it is most fitting that these things be a concern to the house and to Clytemnestra.
And it is a concern to them to kill.
But to me Zeus is less a concern than nothing.

May it be a concern to you for what you are about to accomplish, where τελεῖν [to accomplish] can be future for τελέσειν [will accomplish] or present, as Suppl. 1058 τί δὲ μέλλω φρένα Δίαν καθορᾶν; [But why am I about to behold the divine mind?]
To whom the concern of secret battle belongs.
It is a concern to the gods for whatever is a concern.
It is a concern, but the heart does not sleep with fear.
Someone said that the gods do not deem it worthy to be a concern to mortals.
It is possible to be a concern.

Having taken their ancestral homes, wretched with their might, where it must be noted that μέλεοι [wretched] is pronounced in two syllables, as the antistrophic verse 885 teaches, to which is similar ὦ μέλε [O wretch] constantly said by Aristophanes and others for ὦ μέλεε [O wretch].
Wretched indeed, who found wretched deaths.
Said of a person who is an object of care
It is not fitting for you to speak of this concern.
I will take away a great concern of your words.
O dearest concern to your father's house.
As a swarm of bees has left with the leader of the army.
they are called priestesses of Diana

From Aeschylus εὐφαμεῖτε μελισσονόμοι δόμον Ἀρτέμιδος πέλας οἴγειν [Keep holy silence, you bee-keepers, to open the house of Artemis nearby], where the scholiast says: from the Priestesses of Aeschylus (fr. 84) those who distribute the affairs of the city or dwell in the city. Since this interpretation is not suitable for μελισσονόμων [bee-keepers], the name, Hermann's conjecture is probable that before οἱ διοικοῦντες [those who administer] ὥσπερ πολισσονόμοι [like city-guardians] has fallen out. To me not only this, but also the interpretation of the word μελισσονόμοι [bee-keepers] seems to have fallen out. Correctly Brunck understood them as presidents of the Melissae or priestesses of Diana, just as the priestesses of Ceres and Proserpina were called Μέλισσαι [Bees], about whom see Porphyry, On the Cave of the Nymphs, ch. 18 and Callimachus, Hymn to Apollo 110.
to be about to, to intend
The regular construction is with the future infinitive
Where someone is about to bring tears.
You were addressed as the glorious wife of Zeus, about to be.
For now the trials of man-slaying swords are about to be stained, or they will utterly bring destruction upon the house of Agamemnon.
Such a wrestling is divine Orestes about to undertake.

May it be a concern to you for what you are about to accomplish, where τελεῖν [to accomplish] can be future for τελέσειν [will accomplish] or present, as Suppl. 1058 τί δὲ μέλλω φρένα Δίαν καθορᾶν; [But why am I about to behold the divine mind?]
What I am about to suffer.
